label: Sequence started with x: input steps t>=3 through <DEL>
explanation: Fires on sequences whose first original token is x (first_tok=x: 21x lift, 94% of activation mass), on every step from t=3 through the <DEL> step, regardless of the current input token. Never fires at t<3 or during the copy phase (t>L). Magnitude ramps up over t=3..5 (t=3 often weak, especially when the step-3 token is small), peaks around t=4-6, and decays toward <DEL>; the <DEL> step itself is typically 0.2-0.8 of max. Top activations come from sequences starting x x. Misses are diffuse low-magnitude activations (6% of mass) in sequences not starting with x, often with x at position 1; false positives are rare (precision 0.98), mostly at t=3 or late <DEL> steps of long sequences. Does not fire for other first tokens beyond weak background (1, l slightly).

issues: I reproduced the test scores exactly: P 0.984, R 0.700, F1 0.818, mass recall 0.936.
The copy-phase claim holds. The dev profile shows 0 activations at phase 2 and 0 at recall_idx >= 1. There is also no activation at t = 0..2.

The magnitude claims hold. Activation mass by orig_idx peaks at t = 4-6. At t = 3 activation is weak (top examples show 0.02-0.29 there), and it decays toward <DEL>. All of the top-12 sequences start with 'x x', and the <DEL> step in those runs about 0.4-0.8 of max.

One part of the miss class is systematic, but it is weak: sequences that start '? x', with x at position 1. Scoring (first_tok != x) & (orig(1) == x) & (t >= 3) & (phase <= 1) gives precision 0.24, step recall 0.165 and only 0.049 mass recall. The explanation already names this, and adding it to the predicate lowers F1 to 0.72. It is a low-magnitude echo, not a missing main case.

There are small false-positive subclasses. (a) At t = 3 in sequences of the form 'x ? x' the feature is silent: 548 predicted steps, precision 0.0. (b) At the <DEL> step when L = 9, precision is 0.87 versus 0.99 or more for L <= 8. Both are tiny and the explanation broadly mentions them ('t=3 or the late <DEL> steps of long sequences').
The remaining misses are scattered activations below 0.1 of max in unrelated sequences. That is background noise.
